title: Why he stays in New York; house hunting on Long Island blocked by race
summary: Gil says he feels trapped in New York and describes Long Island landlords refusing to rent to an interracial couple.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well right now, since you've seen so much since you've seen so much both in this Country and other countries, are you in New York because of the artistic need to be here or are you here because the vibration of this city is the one that you like best?

Well really I'm trapped here right now. We have no where to go right now, that's the problem about where to live. I was here for all the reasons you come here to learn more about whatever your trade is. To possibly help iron out some of your emotional problems. And when that's over and you've got what you need from the city, then I think it's time to move on, but I don't know where to go.

You know, when you get aquainted with the market place and all that, you have to do all that first of all, but after you know a eertain amount then you could really live somewhere else and.....

And do your business here. But I don't know where to go because we can't live on Long Island or hardly anywhere on account of the racial problem. We borrowed a, I don't know whether I told you this or not, we borrowed a, a friend of ours in the Village named Casey, who owns Casey's Restaurant, actually he's Chinese and his grandfather is a (Tungsten?) billionnaire. He lent us his chauffeur and limousine and we went out to Long Island to look for a house. And even with the chauffeur and limousine as soon as they saw Anita's brown face they would say they didn't have anything or the owner wouldn't want to rent to us.
I thought money covered everything but even with the chauffeur and limousine it doesn't.
That surprised me you know. So naturally we didn't move to Long Island.

You know that's a difficult place because you've got such a, it's filled now with lower class people who are fighting for their own stability and they are just much too bigoted in most instances and certainly too ignorant.
It's really, everybody is afraid really.
To be over that, yes. And they believe this old fiction about property values going down as soon as.....
It's all based on fear, that's right. The loss of money.
